requirements.statement: The project configures its own ship process, from raising a PR to monitoring CI, fixing, re-verifying, merging and deploying, and one command runs it
Issues identified but not fixed are logged: every finding seen and not fixed is filed once in the declared tracker, or named in the readout where it was not filed (F9)
The code verified is the code shipped: at each push, merge and deploy a deterministic check finds the code byte-identical to the anchor, and any change made while shipping is re-verified
Template scaffolded to .claude/rules/ship.md with no active ship step; default string first among its examples; example run lines for release and platform steps
Ordered steps with parameters, in ship and after-shipping parts, with a bounded repeat (unit test: sequencer parse)
close-issue and file-followups after shipping, in the default, each left out to switch it off
Round count on repeat (default 2: two fix rounds, then a final pass), bar on collect-findings, below-bar filing on file-followups
ship.md is owner-governed; changes only via /ship-setup (manual)
/ship-setup interviews, offers the default string, round count 2 and the significance bar, records a release command where verification.md has none, writes ship.md
Running /ship-setup is the approval; no re-confirmation; never run means only a push
/ship-build resolves the current work the way /implement-trd does
The sequencer hands out steps in order, each after the previous succeeded; wait parks, stop sticks
Shipped means the last ship step succeeded; then after-shipping steps and shipped.json; closed is not shipped
Readout, then COMPLETE or STUCK last; COMPLETE does not mean shipped
No ship.md, or no ship step: commit, push, no PR, point to /ship-setup; name a PR already open
A full PRD to TRD feature needs closed.json; /plan and /sweep do not
Primitive set present; old stages map onto it
Default and five owner strings parse and run end to end (release with an identity command)
open-pr opens against ship.md's base whatever the setting; reuses an open PR
merge, release, run and other outward primitives run only when listed; listing authorizes; release to any environment; pull-request.js still never merges
Release command comes from verification.md, else ship.md; with neither, stop
push commits a sweep by pathspec
Code fixes go via discovered.record and --reconcile --chained; no direct edits; implement-trd.md admits /ship-build
Triage table followed; lint is a tool run
Ownership judge; out-of-scope failures filed, not fixed
Re-verify only criteria whose covered files changed; never re-audit
Significance bar; reviewer labels used when present
repeat rounds=N makes at most N fix rounds (default 2), then one final pass; in it critical stops, below-critical recorded and filed by file-followups
Any wait ends the run COMPLETE with a resumable record; readout says not shipped, NEXT is --resume
--resume runs remaining steps
Close only after the last ship step, in the declared tracker (manual, live)
Close the issue the PRD/TRD header or branch names; none means close nothing and say so
All sources filed, only this work's and this ship's; old sweep-ledger rows untouched
Below-bar not filed unless opted in, including the AC-F9.7 record
Filed issue links back; filed at most once, with a stable id
Unfiled findings listed in readout; below-bar review findings named with the record's path
/implement-trd Step 7.2 records every review finding it did not fix
stack.md template declares the issue tracker
Close and file use the declared tracker
With no tracker, nothing is filed or closed, and the readout lists it
/audit-build names /ship-build and never runs it; PR opening unchanged
constitution.md amendment drafted (manual, owner review)
autonomy.md amendment drafted: listed outward steps authorized, /ship-setup interactive, PR exception kept
Neither constitution.md nor autonomy.md changed before approval (git log review)
Anchor is the audited commit, else the pushed commit
Code equal means no tree difference outside .trd-state/, the audit report, the TRD, and test-only files
Push, merge and deploy links each compare with the anchor
Full commit id written; unique short id resolves, ambiguous fails
Changes to shipped source are re-verified, then the anchor moves; each move is recorded by the custody check alone
Any other difference stops the run naming the step and files; never auto-fixed
Deterministic library with unit tests, outside pull-request.js
A PR trigger resumes the remaining steps (manual, live)
Trigger claimed only when set
The owner's primitives exist; push and the design sync are settled by the TRD (unit test, grep)
Each primitive states its input, result and waiting state with its bounded primitive (unit test: contracts)
The project's string runs under deterministic code (unit test: sequencer)
Iteration is one generic bounded repeat (unit test / code review)
The default string is the template's first example and /ship-setup's default; strings with an approval step or no outside reviewer run on the same code
Primitive or sequencer, never both; a new primitive needs no sequencer change (code review / unit test)
/sync-design runs unasked after merge, via a deterministic check with no Forge assumption (unit test / manual, live)
/ship-build and /ship-setup end with the four-section readout and a COMPLETE or STUCK banner as the last line
No turn claims later work without the primitive that backs it in the same turn; a CI wait uses a bounded primitive
/ship-build runs autonomously from invocation to banner and asks only in autonomy.md's four cases; /ship-setup is interactive by purpose
Ensemble never assumes Forge exists
The chain-of-custody check is deterministic and unit-tested
Last line of every final turn is a COMPLETE or STUCK banner, preceded by the readout (session log)
No unbacked resume, trigger, CI or notification claim (discipline-stop judge; session log)
/ship-build asks only in the four cases; /ship-setup interviews (session log)
No Forge call or assumption in either command (grep / manual)
Unit tests cover each link (push, merge, deploy), the ignored-path classification, each way the anchor moves, and each failure condition (Jest)

tasks.description: Policy file (ship.md template, owner-governed) and the release-command reader; stack.md.template gains ## Issue Tracker; readFullDeploy and BUILD_TOKEN export in functional-verification.js
custody.js chain-of-custody library with CLI and tests against temp git repos, a local bare origin and a stub gh
implement-trd.md and audit-build.md changes (--shipping, /ship-build as --chained caller, Step 7.2 recording rule, full audited commit id, NEXT naming /ship-build) and their pins
verify-build.md: --criteria <ids> and --chained honoured with it; new verify-build-criteria.test.js
ship-sequencer.js (parse, next, record, wait, stop, repeat, shipped, outward-step gate) with CLI and tests over fixture contracts
Post-merge design sync: design-map.js unsynced --merged-into; sync-design.md --chained; Unsynced boards paragraphs in audit-build.md and close-feature.md
pull-request.js ensure --base <branch> --listed with retargeting and its tests
Write docs/plan/ship-build.governance-draft.md (draft only; constitution, autonomy and stack.md read but not changed)
The thirteen primitive contracts under packages/core/contracts/ (plus .claude/contracts/ copies) and ship-primitives.test.js
packages/core/commands/ship-build.md (plus .claude/commands copy), surface test and seam test
ship-setup skill (SKILL.md, tests, vendored copy), framework-skills.txt row, and the F17 trigger-workflow template
Add /ship-build and /ship-setup to process.md, CLAUDE.md, templates, reference docs, init-project command lists, router hint; note in pr-at-cycle-end.md
Apply SHIP-D001's approved draft to constitution.md (and template), autonomy.md (and template), and stack.md. DEFERRED by design.
[LIVE] Owner's live proof on a throwaway GitHub repository. DEFERRED by design.

could_not_verify: TRD Could Not Verify row 1: the wording of ruling J (J-1 to J-7) and the 2026-11-05 post-merge sync scope is the owner's; no record exists outside the TRD and PRD. Check: owner reads J-1 to J-7 against what they ruled, or the relayed message is linked.

TRD Could Not Verify row 2: a Skill-forked /code-review --fix reports each finding, with whether it was applied, back to the session (D25, OQ-10). Check: run /implement-trd on a fixture and inspect what reaches the session after Step 7.2.

TRD Could Not Verify row 3: after a squash or rebase merge, gh pr view --json headRefOid still reports the PR head, and gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged lists the PR (D11, D38, D43). Check: gh pr view and gh pr list on one squash-merged and one rebase-merged PR.
TRD Could Not Verify row 4: Monitor can hold a command run over a gh pr checks loop, re-armed, to completion (D20). Check: one live wait-ci.
TRD Could Not Verify row 5: gh run rerun <id> --failed re-runs only failed jobs and a later check loop sees the result (D16). Check: one live flaky-CI run.
TRD Could Not Verify row 6: gh pr edit --base retargets a PR another command opened without side effects on its reviews (D22). Check: one retarget on a throwaway PR.
TRD Could Not Verify row 7: /implement-trd --reconcile --chained --shipping from /ship-build behaves as --chained does from /audit-build (D14). Check: a fixture session.

TRD Could Not Verify row 8: @coderabbitai review and @codex review request a review, and the bots post as a login containing coderabbit or codex (section 3.2). Check: one PR in a repository with each installed.
TRD Could Not Verify row 9: a headless claude -p '/code-review <pr-url> --comment' posts its findings as PR comments, under the owner's login (OQ-23). Check: one fixture PR.
TRD Could Not Verify row 10: /sync-design --chained, with no build reachable, reports every board uncaptured rather than stopping (section 3.9). Check: a fixture with a design and nothing running.
TRD Could Not Verify row 11: a GitHub Actions workflow can run /ship-build --resume with the plugin and the pushed state (D35). Check: SHIP-T002.

TRD Could Not Verify row 12: each tracker's done state can be found from its CLI without asking the owner (Jira transitions; Linear workflow states) (D28). Check: run jira issues transitions and the linearis state listing on a test project.
TRD Could Not Verify row 13: a workflow script cannot invoke a Skill (D45). Check: the runtime's script API; the Skill limit itself is inferred, not read.
PRD Could Not Verify row 1: the brief's section 10 records the owner's answers verbatim, including the 2026-11-02 simplification. Check: compare section 10 with the /refine-prd session transcripts.

PRD Could Not Verify row 2: the #49 session (2026-10-30): the owner typed Merge it, the agent checked CI and merged by hand, four leftovers unfiled. Check: that session's transcript or the .trd-state/ records for the #49 fix.
PRD Could Not Verify row 3: CodeRabbit labels finding severity, including a critical level (belief, not fact). Check: CodeRabbit documentation or a sample review on a PR.
PRD Could Not Verify row 4: a trigger on a PR (e.g. on approval) can resume /ship-build (belief, not fact). Check: prototype with GitHub Actions or RemoteTrigger.

PRD Could Not Verify row 5: ruling J's words (J-1 to J-7) as TRD 2.0.0 records them are the owner's, relayed; the brief section 10 does not carry them. Check: compare TRD 2.0.0's J rows with the 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06 session transcripts.
PRD Could Not Verify row 6: Codex and a headless Claude Code session can each be requested to review a PR and post findings there (J-1, belief, not fact). Check: one trial PR per reviewer.
PRD Could Not Verify row 7: stack.md drives selection of the managing-* tracker skills. Check: read skill-selection-instructions.md and scaffold-project.sh's skill selection.

PRD Could Not Verify row 8: managing-linear-issues, managing-jira-issues and gh each support creating and closing issues (only the Azure DevOps skill was read). Check: read each packages/skills/managing-*/SKILL.md.

PRD Could Not Verify row 9: discovered.jsonl non-blocking rows are distinguishable from blocking ones for filing (blocksFeature is stored by discovered.js). Check: read discovered.js read/filter functions.

PRD Could Not Verify row 10: a deployed environment exposes a way to read its build identity, for the deploy link (per-project infrastructure). Check: ask per project at /ship-setup; verification.md section 2 has no production row.

PRD Could Not Verify row 11: after a squash or rebase merge, GitHub still records the PR head commit (headRefOid), so the merge link can compare its code (belief, not fact). Check: gh pr view on one squash-merged and one rebase-merged PR.
